relations.myth: Joseph prospers and preserves life through divine providence
relations.note: God grants Joseph favor, dream interpretation, authority, and the means to preserve life.
Joseph is Jacob's favored son by Rachel.

relations.myth: Jacob gives Joseph the distinctive robe
relations.note: Jacob favors Joseph and gives him the robe that provokes his brothers' jealousy.
Joseph sends his shirt, which restores his father's sight before their reunion.
Rachel is Joseph's mother; she dies before his adult story begins.
Benjamin is Joseph's full brother, sharing both Jacob and Rachel as parents.

relations.myth: Joseph plants the cup in Benjamin's sack
relations.note: Joseph secretly plants his cup and detains Benjamin to test their brothers.
Reuben is Joseph's paternal half-brother.

relations.myth: Reuben attempts to save Joseph from murder
relations.note: Reuben redirects the brothers toward the pit, intending to return Joseph safely to Jacob.
Simeon is Joseph's paternal half-brother.

relations.myth: Joseph binds Simeon as a hostage
relations.note: Joseph imprisons Simeon until the brothers return to Egypt with Benjamin.
Levi is Joseph's paternal half-brother; no individual encounter is narrated.
Judah is Joseph's paternal half-brother.
Judah persuades the brothers to sell Joseph rather than kill him.

relations.myth: Judah offers himself and Joseph reveals his identity
relations.note: Judah's plea to replace Benjamin moves Joseph to reveal himself to his brothers.
Dan is Joseph's paternal half-brother; no individual interaction is narrated.
Naphtali is Joseph's paternal half-brother; Genesis narrates no individual interaction.
Gad is Joseph's paternal half-brother; no individual encounter is narrated.
Asher is Joseph's paternal half-brother; no individual encounter is narrated.
Issachar is Joseph's paternal half-brother; no individual encounter is narrated.
Zebulun is Joseph's paternal half-brother; no individual encounter is narrated.
Potiphar purchases Joseph and appoints him steward over his household.

relations.myth: Potiphar imprisons Joseph after the accusation
relations.note: Potiphar has Joseph imprisoned after hearing his wife's allegation.
She repeatedly demands sex from Joseph, who refuses and flees.

relations.myth: The rejected wife falsely accuses Joseph
relations.note: She uses Joseph's abandoned garment to accuse him of attempted sexual assault.
Later Islamic literature names the master's wife and expands her pursuit of Joseph.
Persian romance makes the restored, repentant Zulaykhā Joseph's lawful wife.
Asenath is Joseph's Egyptian wife and the mother of Manasseh and Ephraim.

relations.myth: Asenath converts and becomes Joseph's heavenly bride
relations.note: The romance expands their marriage into Asenath's conversion and a conspiracy against the couple.
Manasseh is Joseph's first son by Asenath.
Ephraim is Joseph's second son by Asenath.
Machir is Joseph's grandson through Manasseh.
Shuthelah is listed among Joseph's descendants through Ephraim.
Beriah is listed among Joseph's descendants through Ephraim.

relations.myth: Moses carries Joseph's bones from Egypt
relations.note: Moses fulfills Joseph's oath by carrying his remains during the Exodus.

relations.myth: Gabriel directs Joseph toward his brothers
relations.note: Later interpretation identifies Joseph's unnamed guide near Shechem as the angel Gabriel.
Christian exegesis typologically parallels Joseph's betrayal, suffering, salvation, and exaltation with Christ.
Joseph descends from Abraham and professes adherence to his ancestral religion.
Joseph is Isaac's grandson and names him among the ancestral prophets he follows.
